issues.suggestion: Every edition ends the geopolitics section with an oil price update in the same sentence structure ('O Brent [verb] $X'). This has become a predictable coda. Vary the framing — lead with the policy response (Fed, Trump sanctions) and embed the price as context, or frame around cumulative impact (e.g. 'oil has risen X% in four days') instead of a new spot price.

issues.suggestion: Benchmark score drops as proof of superiority is a recurring pattern — MiniMax on 03-19, LangChain and MiroMind on 03-16. Readers start glazing over percentages. For at least one of these, describe what the model actually does differently instead of citing scores.

issues.current_text: Do outro lado da moeda, um agente autônomo da Meta disparou um incidente Sev-1
issues.suggestion: The 'good AI news then flip to bad AI news' pivot with a transition phrase ('Do outro lado da moeda') is a recognizable rhetorical device. The Uber-then-Meta juxtaposition is good editorial instinct, but the connector phrase is a crutch. Let the contrast speak for itself or use a harder cut.

summary: Moderate repetition: DOD-Anthropic replacement is a retread from yesterday, GTC/HBM4 callbacks to 03-16, and the oil-price coda + Nature-breakthrough + benchmark-score framings have become formulaic across editions.
